Sample: Typing Rules for a Ruby Core Calculus

September 16, 2026

This is a sample post for testing how type judgements and inference rules render. The calculus below is a toy, not the real formalization.

Syntax

Expressions e range over variables, self, integer literals, nil, method calls, object construction, sequencing, and conditionals:

e::=x∣self∣n∣nil∣e.m(e―)∣C.new∣e1;e2∣if e1 then e2 else e3τ::=C∣Nil∣τ1∪τ2

A typing judgement Γ⊢e:τ says that under environment Γ, expression e has type τ.

Typing Rules

Axioms have an empty premise:

Γ(x)=τΓ⊢x:τ (T-Var)Γ⊢n:Integer (T-Int)Γ⊢nil:Nil (T-Nil)

Rules with several premises separate them with \quad:

Γ⊢e1:τ1Γ⊢e2:τ2Γ⊢e1;e2:τ2 (T-Seq) Γ⊢e1:τ1Γ⊢e2:τ2Γ⊢e3:τ3Γ⊢if e1 then e2 else e3:τ2∪τ3 (T-If)

Method calls look up a signature in the class table CT:

Γ⊢e0:Cmtype(CT,C,m)=τ―→τΓ⊢e―:τ′―τ′―<:τ―Γ⊢e0.m(e―):τ (T-Call)

Subsumption:

Γ⊢e:ττ<:τ′Γ⊢e:τ′ (T-Sub)

Subtyping

τ<:τ (S-Refl)τ1<:τ2τ2<:τ3τ1<:τ3 (S-Trans)CT(C)=class C<D {…}C<:D (S-Class) τ1<:τ1∪τ2 (S-UnionL)τ1<:ττ2<:ττ1∪τ2<:τ (S-UnionE)

A Derivation Tree

Nested fractions give full derivations. Here is a proof that x:Integer⊢x;nil:Integer∪Nil:

Γ(x)=IntegerΓ⊢x:IntegerΓ⊢nil:NilΓ⊢x;nil:NilNil<:Integer∪NilΓ⊢x;nil:Integer∪Nil

Operational Semantics

A small-step relation ⟨e,σ⟩⟶⟨e′,σ′⟩ over expressions and heaps:

⟨e1,σ⟩⟶⟨e1′,σ′⟩⟨e1;e2,σ⟩⟶⟨e1′;e2,σ′⟩ (E-Seq)v is a value⟨v;e2,σ⟩⟶⟨e2,σ⟩ (E-SeqV)

Soundness

Theorem (Progress). If ∅⊢e:τ and σ is well-typed, then either e is a value or there exist e′ and σ′ such that ⟨e,σ⟩⟶⟨e′,σ′⟩.

Theorem (Preservation). If Γ⊢e:τ and ⟨e,σ⟩⟶⟨e′,σ′⟩, then Γ⊢e′:τ.
